# Streaming Koenker studentized Breusch\\–Pagan test

<small>Source: [`R/performance.R`](https://github.com/DiogoRibeiro7/heteroTests/blob/main/R/performance.R) · Help: `?performKoenkerTestStreaming`</small>

Evaluates Koenker's studentized variant of the Breusch\\–Pagan test (the
\(n R^2\) statistic from regressing the squared residuals on the regressors)
using streamed cross-products so that large datasets can be processed without
allocating the full auxiliary regression matrix.

## Usage

```r
performKoenkerTestStreaming(
  model,
  data = NULL,
  chunk_size = 10000,
  progress = interactive()
)
```

## Arguments

`model`
:   A fitted [stats::lm](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/lm.html) object supplying residuals and fitted values for
    the diagnostic.

`data`
:   A [base::data.frame](https://rdrr.io/r/base/data.frame.html) containing the variables referenced in
    `model`. The data must align with the observations used to fit the model. When `NULL`, the default, the model frame of `model` is used. It holds the terms of the model rather than its variables (`log(x)` rather than `x`), so a model that transforms a variable needs `data`, as does a model with an `offset()` term, and so may a fit whose `weights` or `offset` argument is a column of the data, which the model frame holds as `(weights)` or `(offset)`.

`chunk_size`
:   Positive integer giving the number of observations processed per
    streaming chunk.

`progress`
:   Logical flag indicating whether a textual progress bar should be shown
    while processing the chunks. Defaults to `interactive()`.

## Value

A `htest` object equivalent to [`performKoenkerTest`](performKoenkerTest.md) with metadata
recording the streaming configuration.

## Details

Chunks of the data contribute to the cross-product matrices for the regression
of squared residuals on the model regressors. Aggregating these matrices yields
the exact Koenker statistic while bounding memory usage. Sparse cross-products
from Matrix are used automatically when available for large chunks.

## Supported models

It accepts an `lm` and a `glm` with the Gaussian family and the identity link, unweighted
or with positive weights, a `fitWLS()` fit and, since 0.16.0, a rank-deficient fit, which it
tests on the estimable part of its design: it gives the value of the same model fitted without the
aliased columns. It refuses a `glm` of another family or link, a `survey::svyglm()` fit, a
fit with a zero weight, a coefficient that is not finite for another reason, and `data` that
lack rows or variables of the fit. Which model each test accepts, and why, is set out in
[`test_results`](test_results.md), under *Supported models*.

## See also

[`performKoenkerTest`](performKoenkerTest.md) for the standard implementation.

## Examples

```r
data(mtcars)
mod <- lm(mpg ~ wt + qsec, data = mtcars)
performKoenkerTestStreaming(mod, mtcars, chunk_size = 16, progress = FALSE)
```
